# kamishibai

> kamishibai turns a list of words into an illustrated Anki deck — one card per word with a native example sentence, native-speaker audio, and a manga-style panel — using Google Gemini. It runs as an interactive terminal UI or as an asynchronous, session-based console flow built for agents.

This file documents the **console (session) flow**. Running `kamishibai` with no arguments opens the interactive TUI instead, which is out of scope here.

A session is a persistent, curatable unit of work an agent drives across separate invocations. It moves through stages:

1. **understood** — `new` understands each `--word` (or imports a cards JSON) and creates the session. The session now holds curatable candidates: per word, the senses the model proposed.
2. **(curate)** — optional: `select` which senses become cards, `exclude` a word, or `correct` a word to add senses. Each keeps the session understood.
3. **generating** — `generate` commits the curated plan and starts a managed background worker that produces the artifacts and publishes.
4. **published** — every committed card made the deck. `result` returns the finished cards; `regenerate` re-rolls committed cards.

A run where some cards exhaust their retries ends **partial** — the deck holds the rest, and `regenerate --failed` fills the gaps. A run where no card survives ends **failed**.

Commands may run concurrently: edits serialize and all apply, and only one worker can generate a session at a time (a second `generate`, or any edit while one runs, is refused until it finishes or is cancelled).

Generation is slow (Gemini per artifact, and the first publish parses system fonts for the PDF — expect tens of seconds). Poll `status` at a relaxed interval; do not tight-loop. Re-running is idempotent and cache-backed, so a killed `generate` resumes and only fills in what is missing. The interactive TUI (`kamishibai` with no arguments, or `kamishibai open [<id>]`) shares this same session model, so `ls`/`status` see interactive runs too.

## Output contract

There are exactly **two modes**:

- **plain text (default)** — for humans. Readable, line-oriented; not a parsing target.
- **`--json` (placed after the verb)** — for machines. Exactly one JSON document per invocation on stdout.

If you are an agent, **use `--json`**. Do not scrape plain text — it has no machine-stable contract and prints nothing bare to capture.

- Every single-session command opens its plain output with one header line: `your session <ID> · <KNOWN> → <LEARNING> · <phase>`. The id lives there, once.
- **Language codes are UPPERCASE** everywhere in output — ids (`FR-…`), the pair (`EN → FR`), card-side labels (`FR:`/`EN:`), the cache layout (`cards/EN-FR`), and deck filenames (`FR_….apkg`) — and in JSON (`"known":"EN"`, `"lang":"FR"`). **Input accepts any case** and is normalised to uppercase.
- Errors are one `kamishibai: <message>` line plus one next-step hint line on stderr (in both modes). In `--json` mode the machine-readable envelope is additionally printed on stdout.
- Plain read/mutate output goes to stdout; the `generate --wait` / `regenerate --wait` progress stream goes to stderr.
- Exit codes are the script signal: `0` ok · `2` usage · `3` no such session · `4` not ready yet · `5` ambiguous (an omitted id matched several sessions) · `1` other error. **For any invocation accepted in both modes they are identical — `--json` changes representation, never the signal, locking, idempotency, or session semantics.** `open` is interactive and refuses `--json` (exit `2`). clap parse errors (unknown flag, `--json` placed before the verb) stay plain text outside the envelope.

### Omitting the session id

Every verb's `<id>` is optional, so a single-session workflow never needs to capture or pass one — run `new`, then `generate`, then `status`/`result` with no id. When omitted, the command resolves the session once, at invocation: if exactly one session exists it is used (even a finished one); otherwise, if exactly one session is **unfinished** (`understood`/`generating`/`interrupted` — anything except `published`/`partial`/`failed`/`cancelled`) it is used; otherwise nothing runs, the command exits `5`, and prints `kamishibai: N unfinished sessions — pass an id (see kamishibai ls)` followed by the newest five as `ls` lines (in `--json` mode the envelope carries them in a `sessions` array). With no sessions at all it exits `3`. The cascade prefers the session you are working on, not the one that is done: with a published deck and a fresh understood session, `result` resolves to the fresh one and exits `4` — pass the id to read an older session's result.

### JSON mode

`--json` prints exactly one document per invocation on stdout — the success document, or on any failure the error envelope `{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"usage|not_found|not_ready|ambiguous|operational","exit":2|3|4|5|1,"message":"…"}}`. The `ambiguous` envelope additionally carries a top-level `sessions` array — the newest five candidates, same item shape as `ls --json`. The schema evolves additively only: keys are never renamed or removed. The document carries **only data** — no derived counts or state words; compute those from `artifacts` + `phase`.

Every stateful verb (`new`, `select`, `exclude`, `correct`, `generate`, `regenerate`, `cancel`, `status`) returns the same **session document** — mutating verbs return the post-mutation state, so no follow-up `status` is needed:

```json
{"ok":true,"session":"FR-20260612_091500_ab3x","created":"2026-06-12T09:15:00Z",
 "pair":{"known":"EN","learning":"FR"},"senses":"primary","source":"words",
 "out":"/abs/out","phase":"generating",
 "worker":{"pid":4242,"alive":true},
 "progress":{"term":"canard","artifact":"scene"},
 "candidates":{"items":[
   {"term":"canard","included":true,"senses":[
     {"tag":"zool.","understanding":"a duck","selected":true},
     {"understanding":"a hoax","selected":false}]}]},
 "cards":{"items":[
   {"term":"canard","understanding":"a duck",
    "artifacts":{"meta":true,"sound":true,"scene":false,"picture":false}}]},
 "result":{"deck":"/o/FR.apkg","pdf":"/o/FR.pdf","dir":"/o"}}
```

Presence rules: `phase` is the live reconciliation (one of `understood`/`generating`/`published`/`partial`/`failed`/`interrupted`/`cancelled`); `candidates` appears while the record holds curatable candidates, `cards` once a plan is committed, and `worker`/`progress`/`result`/`error` only when present — absent fields are omitted, never `null`. `progress` appears only while `generating`. A sense's 1-based position in its `senses` array is its `select --sense` number. A card's state is derived: `meta`→`sound`→`scene`→`picture` is strictly sequential, so a card with all four `artifacts` true is in the deck, and the first false artifact is where it stands (in work under `generating`, where it failed under `failed`/`partial`).

Other shapes: `result --json` → `{"ok":true,"session":…,"pair":…,"phase":…,"paths":{"deck":…,"pdf":…,"dir":…},"failed":M,"items":[…]}` where `items` are strict cards-JSON entries — the exact `new --build` schema (with uppercase `lang`), so they round-trip into a new session. `ls --json` → `{"ok":true,"sessions":[{"id":…,"pair":…,"created":…,"phase":…,"cards":{"total":N,"ready":M}}]}` (`"selected":N` instead of `cards` before a plan is committed; the array may be empty). `rm --json` → `{"ok":true,"removed":"<id>"}`. `cache-path --json` → `{"ok":true,"cache":"/…"}`. `config --json` → `{"ok":true,"known":"EN","key_saved":bool}` (`known` omitted until one is saved; the key value is never returned).

`generate --wait --json` streams NDJSON **events on stderr** and prints the one final session document on stdout (`published` or `partial`; a run where every card failed exits `1` with the error envelope instead — `status <id> --json` then shows `"phase":"failed"`; a cancel that raced in yields `ok:true` with `"phase":"cancelled"` and no `result`, so gate on `phase`, not `ok`). Events: `{"event":"generating","cards":N}`, `{"event":"step","term":…,"artifact":"meta|sound|scene|picture","status":"ok|cache|retry|fail","attempt":1,"ceiling":3}` (attempt/ceiling only on retry/fail), `{"event":"publishing"}`, `{"event":"warning","message":…}`. stderr lines that do not parse as JSON are lower-layer narration (model downloads etc.) — ignore them; strictness is guaranteed only for stdout.

## Requirements

- A Gemini API key is required for any flow that calls Gemini: set `GEMINI_API_KEY` (it wins), or save one with `kamishibai config --key` (or the interactive Welcome screen). `GEMINI_API_KEY` need not be set when a saved key exists.
- The first OCR-backed run downloads PP-OCRv5 model files into the cache.

## Commands

Every session verb also accepts `--json` (after the verb).

- `kamishibai new (--word WORD [--word WORD …] | --words FILE | --build FILE) [--learning LANG] [--known LANG] [--senses primary|all] [--out DIR] [--id NAME] [--generate]` — understand the words and create a session in the **understood** stage. Exactly one input form is required: repeated `--word` flags (one card per word), `--words FILE` (one word per line, `-` for stdin), or `--build FILE` (a strict cards JSON path or `-`, skips understanding; its entries carry the language pair, so `--known`/`--learning`/`--senses` are rejected with it). `--senses` sets the initial sense selection (`primary` = the top sense; `all` = every sense); `select` overrides it later. `--generate` commits and starts the worker at once. `--learning` is autodetected from the words when omitted — pass it only to force a specific language; `--known` is a one-off override resolved from your saved preference and **refused** (exit 2) when neither is set — save it once with `config --known`.
- `kamishibai select [<id>] --card TERM --sense 1,3` — choose which 1-based senses of a card become cards (and re-include it). Resets the session to understood.
- `kamishibai exclude [<id>] --card TERM` — drop a card from the plan while keeping it visible in the understanding. Resets to understood.
- `kamishibai correct [<id>] --card TERM --note "..."` — ask Gemini to add senses to a card from an instruction. Resets to understood.
- `kamishibai generate [<id>] [--wait]` — commit the curated plan (deriving it from the selected senses) and start a managed background worker that generates the missing artifacts then publishes; returns at once. `--wait` runs it in the foreground, streaming progress. Fails if nothing is selected.
- `kamishibai status [<id>]` — before a plan is committed: the curatable candidates with their senses and selection; after: per-card artifact progress. Read from the cache (no Gemini).
- `kamishibai open [<id>]` — open the session in the interactive TUI, resuming from the cache.
- `kamishibai result [<id>]` — the finished cards (term, meaning, both example sentences, transcription, hint), the deck/pdf/dir paths, and the per-card asset cache folder. Works once the session is **published** or **partial**; exits `4` otherwise. For a path in a script, use `result --json` (e.g. `.paths.deck`).
- `kamishibai regenerate [<id>] (--failed | --card TERM [--note "..."]) [--wait]` — re-roll committed cards: drop the cached artifacts of every unfinished card (`--failed`) or one card (`--card`), then immediately regenerate and republish (it runs a worker just like `generate`). With `--note`, Gemini first rewrites that card from the instruction before the rebuild. Returns like `generate`: at once for a detached run, the terminal session document after `--wait`.
- `kamishibai cancel [<id>]` — stop the running worker (leaves an already-finished session — published/partial/failed — unchanged). Always exits `0` with a correct final phase, even when it races the worker finishing.
- `kamishibai ls` — list sessions, one per line: `<id>  <KNOWN> → <LEARNING>  <phase>  <progress>` (`-- / N` before a plan is committed, `ready/total` after).
- `kamishibai rm [<id>] [--cache]` — delete the session, and with `--cache` its cached card folders.
- `kamishibai cache-path` — print the cache directory.
- `kamishibai config [--known LANG] [--key KEY]` — save console defaults to preferences, or show them with no flags. `--known` is validated against the catalog and saved uppercase; `--key` is verified against Gemini before saving (`-` reads it from stdin, `""` clears it). The key value is never returned.

Supported language codes (any case accepted): `en`, `zh`, `es`, `ja`, `fr`, `de`, `ru`, `it`, `pt`, `el`.

## Example renderings (plain text, for humans)

`kamishibai new --word flâner --word canard --known en --learning fr`:

```
your session FR-20260614_091239_397s · EN → FR · understood
I understood 2 words. * = the sense that becomes a card.
words:
  flâner
    * 1 to stroll, to wander aimlessly with no destination
  canard
    * 1 a duck, the waterbird
      2 (colloq.) a newspaper, especially a low-quality one
Change a card: kamishibai select canard --sense 2 (or drop it: kamishibai exclude canard)
Generate: kamishibai generate
```

`kamishibai status <id>` while **generating**:

```
your session FR-20260614_091239_397s · EN → FR · generating
building 2 cards (pid 48213)
  flâner meaning ✓ audio ✓ scene ✓ picture ✓
  canard meaning ✓ audio ✓ scene · picture ·
out: /Users/you/kamishibai-out
```

`kamishibai result <id>` once **published**:

```
your session FR-20260614_091239_397s · EN → FR · published
all 2 cards are in the deck
deck: /Users/you/kamishibai-out/FR_2026-06-14_091412.apkg
pdf: /Users/you/kamishibai-out/FR_2026-06-14_091412.pdf
dir: /Users/you/kamishibai-out
cache: /Users/you/Library/Caches/kamishibai/cards/EN-FR
  flâner · importance 7
    meaning: to stroll, to wander aimlessly
    say: flɑ.ne
    FR: J'aime flâner le long de la Seine le dimanche après-midi.
    EN: I love to «stroll» along the Seine on Sunday afternoons.
    hint: unhurried, pleasure-led walking, never commuting.
```

`generate --wait` streams progress on stderr, then the paths:

```
your session FR-20260614_091239_397s · EN → FR · generating
  flâner · meaning ✓
  flâner · audio ✓
  canard · picture · retry 1/3
  canard · picture ✓
done:
/Users/you/kamishibai-out/FR_2026-06-14_091412.apkg
/Users/you/kamishibai-out/FR_2026-06-14_091412.pdf
/Users/you/kamishibai-out
```

## Driving it from a script (use `--json`)

A single-session workflow needs no id — omit it everywhere and let resolution find the session:

```
kamishibai new --word flâner --word canard --known en --learning fr --json >/dev/null
kamishibai exclude --card canard --json >/dev/null     # optional curation
kamishibai generate --json >/dev/null                  # detached worker
while :; do
  phase=$(kamishibai status --json | jq -r .phase)
  case "$phase" in
    published) break ;;
    partial)   echo "some cards failed; the deck is partial" >&2; break ;;
    failed|interrupted|cancelled) echo "generation did not finish" >&2; exit 1 ;;
    *) sleep 5 ;;
  esac
done
deck=$(kamishibai result --json | jq -r .paths.deck)
```

`phase` can be any of `understood`/`generating`/`published`/`partial`/`failed`/`interrupted`/`cancelled`, so a poll loop must break on every terminal phase, not just `published`, or it spins forever on a failed run. To capture an id explicitly, read `.session` from any verb's `--json` document.

## Cache

The cache directory is printed by `kamishibai cache-path` (macOS `~/Library/Caches/kamishibai`; Linux `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/kamishibai` or `~/.cache/kamishibai`; override with `KAMISHIBAI_CACHE`). Preferences (saved language and key) live under the data home (macOS `~/Library/Application Support/kamishibai`; Linux `$XDG_DATA_HOME` or `~/.local/share/kamishibai`); override with `KAMISHIBAI_DATA`.

```
<cache>/cards/<KNOWN>-<LEARNING>/<key>/      meta.json  scene.json  voice.wav  illustration.jpg
<cache>/understanding/<KNOWN>-<LEARNING>/<key>.json
<cache>/sessions/<id>/                session.json  worker.log
<cache>/ocr-models/                   shared OCR model files
```

`<key>` is a short content hash. `status` derives each card's readiness by checking which artifact files exist; deleting a card's folder forces it to regenerate on the next `generate`. `session.json` additionally holds the typed words, the curated candidates, and the committed plan.

## Input

For `new` each word is one `--word` flag (one card per word); `--words FILE` reads one word per line and `--words -` reads stdin.

For `new --build FILE` the input is a strict cards JSON path (or `-` for stdin). Every field is required and unknown fields are rejected:

```json
{
  "entries": [
    {
      "term": "lantern",
      "meaning": "a portable lamp",
      "pronunciation": "LAN-tern",
      "transcription": "/lantern/",
      "importance": 7,
      "source": {
        "sentence": "I carried a lantern through the dark hallway.",
        "lang": "en",
        "highlight": "lantern",
        "hint": "portable light",
        "context": "a simple everyday sentence"
      },
      "target": { "sentence": "Ich trug eine Laterne durch den dunklen Flur.", "lang": "de" }
    }
  ]
}
```

`importance` is an integer 1–10; text fields and language codes must be non-empty. Language codes are accepted in any case (`en` or `EN`) and normalised to uppercase in the session.
